{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Dessert|Dessert]] | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Brazil|Brazilian Cuisine]]

'''Brigadeiro''' is a simple Brazilian chocolate fudge candy created in the 1920s. It is named after Brazilian airman  Eduardo Gomes (''brigadeiro'' being his rank in the Air Force). It's commonly served with soda, coffee or milk.
== Ingredients ==

* 1 can (395 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) of [[Cookbook:Sweetened Condensed Milk|sweetened condensed milk]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoon]] of [[cookbook:butter|butter]]
* 3 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoon]]s of [[Cookbook:Cocoa powder|cocoa powder]]
* 1 box (482 g) of [[Cookbook:Sprinkles|chocolate sprinkles]] 

== Procedure ==

# In a heavy [[cookbook:saucepan|saucepan]], combine the milk, cocoa powder, and butter. Stir to dissolve the chocolate.
# Put over low heat and stir constantly to avoid formation of lumps.
# Continue stirring for 10–12 minutes, or until you are able to see the bottom of the pot for one second when you scratch it side-to-side with the spoon. The more you cook, the harder the resulting candy will be—it may vary from liquid fudge to hard candy.
# Allow mixture to cool.
# Butter your hands, and roll the mixture into small balls (around 2 [[Cookbook:Centimetre (cm)|cm]] in diameter). Alternatively, you can use two metal spoons to shape the candies. Roll them in the chocolate sprinkles.  

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Should you accidentally get hard candy, fill the pot with water and leave to rest—the candy will dissolve completely and the pot will be easy to clean.
* You can substitute 100 g of baking chocolate for the cocoa powder. If you want a lighter candy, use powdered chocolate (such as Nestlé Quick). You can also put [[cookbook:raisin|raisin]]s or [[Cookbook:Nut|nut]]s in the center of the candy. You can decorate with powdered [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]] instead, or cocoa powder.
* Brazilian brigadeiros also have gourmet varieties. Some references are available in specialized houses in Brazil: [http://www.mariabrigadeiro.com.br Maria Brigadeiro] and [http://www.brigadeirissimo.com.br Brigadeiríssimo] and [http://www.BrigadeiroGourmet.com Brigadeiro Gourmet]
